newsitem.title: USA: Chartwell completes Canada hotel deal.
newsitem.headline: Chartwell completes Canada hotel deal.

text.p: Chartwell Leisure Inc said on Friday it bought 20 Travelodge properties in Canada, and a 50 percent joint venture interest in an additional property in Edmonton in a transaction valued at about $70 million.
The company also said in a statement a subsidiary acquired exclusive franchise rights, or a so-called master license, for Travelodge in Canada from Travelodge Hotels Inc, a unit of HFS Inc.
Chartwell said it completed the acquisition of the Travelodge properties from Capital Properties Limited Partnership.

The company said its Chartwell Canada Hospitality Corp subsidiary would operate as a joint venture between Chartwell Leisure and Canadian hotel management and franchise company Royco Hotels and Resorts LTD.
Royco, based in Calgary, Alberta, would also manage the newly acquired Canadian properties, the company said. These hotels had a total of 3,466 rooms.

Chartwell Leisure Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Richard Fisher said: "These steps, including our newly announced master license acquired from HFS, give us a significant presence in the growing Canadian market and will be a springboard for developing and acquiring new properties in Canada, as well as selling additional Travelodge franchises in Canada."

The 75 Canadian Travelodge franchises would be assigned to Chartwell Canada Hospitality Corp, the company said. This unit would administer the licenses and provide franchise services. Reservation services would still be provided by HFS Canada.

Travelodge Hotels Inc is a hotel franchisor. It has over 500 upper economy Travelodge and budget Thriftlodge franchise properties with over 43,000 guest rooms throughout Canada, Latin America and the United States.
